author: Temminck, 1836
summary: 한반도 전역에서 흔히 번식하는 텃새로, 숲 속 나무 위에서 생활한다. 번식기에는 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 다니고, 가을과 겨울에는 혼성 무리를 지어 숲속을 돌아다닌다. 활엽수림이나 잡목림의 큰키나무 줄기에 스스로 구멍을 파 둥지를 짓고, 5월 상순~6월 중순에 한배에 알을 5~7개 낳는다. 곤충과 나무 열매를 먹으며, 국외에서는 중국 북동부, 우수리, 사할린, 쿠릴 열도 남부 등지에 분포한다.

art.subject: Japanese Pygmy Woodpecker (Dendrocopos kizuki), adult male: crown, nape and hindneck grey-brown; a tiny red streak at each side of the rear crown, often hidden; lores and ear-coverts smoky brown; a white stripe behind the eye above the ear-coverts and a white band below them; mantle, back and wings dark brown crossed by many narrow white bars; underparts dull buffy white with fine brown streaks on the breast and flanks; tail blackish, the outer feathers barred white; short lead-grey bill; reddish-brown iris; lead-grey legs.
art.pose: clinging to a tree trunk, chiselling a nest hole
art.scene: Korean broadleaf and scrub woodland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging upright to a trunk, braced on its tail: grey-brown crown and hindneck with a small red streak at the side of the nape, smoky-brown ear patch between white stripes, white-barred dark brown back, streaked buffy underparts, white-barred outer tail feathers, reddish eye, grey legs
adult female, head detail in side profile: grey-brown crown and nape with no red at all, smoky-brown ear patch, white stripe behind the eye, short grey bill
art.build: Tiny woodpecker, about the size of a House Sparrow, one of the smallest woodpeckers in Korea. Rounded head, compact body. Bill short, straight and chisel-tipped, shorter than the head, lead-grey. Legs short, grey, with two toes forward and two back for clinging. Wings rounded, covering most of the back at rest. Tail short, stiff and pointed, used as a prop against the trunk. Creeps along thin branches and trunks, often with mixed flocks of tits; flight bounding.
avoid: Do not paint the pied black-and-white plumage, large white shoulder patches or red undertail of Great Spotted Woodpecker.
Do not paint a red crown or a large red nape patch; the male's red is a tiny streak, often hidden.
Do not paint a long bill; the bill is short and stubby.
Do not paint a black crown or a black back; the crown is grey-brown and the back dark brown barred white.
